desk_desc: Running, and only acting when there's a reason to.

receipts.headline: We put up an honest public face
receipts.lesson: We published this site and said plainly there's one live product, not a portfolio — and the agents build, deploy and maintain the site themselves.

receipts.headline: We gave security a front door
receipts.lesson: We added a public security-disclosure contact, so anyone who spots a problem can tell us — quietly and early, before it becomes one.

receipts.headline: We made our own website heal itself
receipts.lesson: A site that claims a company runs itself must not go stale — so it now rebuilds from the record and speaks up only when it genuinely can't fix itself.

receipts.headline: We decided how we'd be proven wrong, first
receipts.lesson: Before running a test of one of our own ideas, we committed the pass/fail rule to the record — so when the answer came back "no", we couldn't argue with it.

receipts.headline: We broke our own system on purpose
receipts.lesson: We injected faults into the live system to see if it would tell on itself; the health report came back FAILED, which was exactly the result we wanted.
